title: Model onboarding compatibility pact for production handshake
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Define a machine- and human-readable compatibility pact used at model onboarding time that guarantees stable input shapes, canonical prompt variants, parameter aliases, and minimum performance profiles for any model that will be pinned for production use.
rationale: Teams have observed silent regressions when swapping model binaries or minor releases. This ticket creates an explicit onboarding artifact (the 'compatibility pact') that runtime, console, and SDKs can validate against before treating a model as a locked/production variant. The pact reduces incidents, simplifies customer-facing guarantees, and accelerates rollouts.
scope: Schema for the compatibility pact: input signature, allowed prompt templates, canonical parameter names and aliases, expected tokenization behavior
Performance profile section: 50th/95th latency baselines at canonical batch sizes and sequence lengths, per-token throughput, memory footprint bounds
Validation tooling: onboarding CLI check that emits a human-readable report and machine-assertable artifact
Integration points: Redwood runtime check during deploy, Console onboarding checklist, SDK warnings when parameter aliases are used
Regression harness hooks: reference prompts and golden-output fingerprints for semantic stability checks
non_goals: Replacing full behavioral evals or quality assessments (those remain separate),
Guaranteeing semantic equivalence for every prompt across model major versions
Automating model fixes or retraining; this ticket focuses on contract definition and validation only
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility pact JSON Schema accepted by runtime and Console teams
Onboarding CLI produces a pass/fail result and a human-readable report with at least 5 checks
Runtime rejects a deployment of a model marked as 'locked' if the pact validation fails with a clear error code
Console shows the pact status and highlights parameter alias mappings and perf deltas relative to baseline
At least one model has been onboarded using the pact (integration trial) and logged in the onboarding audit dashboard
test_plan: Unit tests for schema validation and alias resolution (coverage > 90%)
End-to-end test: simulate onboarding flow for open-model-XYZ with canonical prompts and assert runtime acceptance
Performance smoke test: run 1k requests at canonical batch size and compare median/95th to declared profile within thresholds
Negative test: intentionally mutate prompt tokenization rules and ensure validation fails and provides actionable diffs
Monitoring: add synthetic checks to CI that validate pact parsing for every release of runtime-1.20
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable pact validation for non-critical internal orgs and require advisory warnings (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (enforced): runtime rejects locked-model deploys that fail validation; Console surfaces blocking messages (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (customer opt-in): add onboarding checklist in Console and allow customers to opt into strict enforcement (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (default): enforcement enabled for newly created dedicated/private clusters; guidance docs published
instrumentation: Onboarding dashboard tile: pact pass rate, top failing checks, and time-to-fix
Runtime metric: pact_validation_failures_total (labels: check, model, org)
Alert: >5% failing canary validations in 24h triggers paging to infra
Audit log entries for each onboarding attempt (linkable to Console session and GitHub PR if provided)
open_questions: What is the canonical list of prompt templates we ship as examples for each model family?
How strict should tokenization invariants be for models that use different tokenizers but claim semantic parity?
Should we version the pact schema independently of runtime releases? (proposal: yes, semver-like)
How to represent tolerated perf degradation ranges vs hard ceilings in the pact?
decisions: Use JSON Schema draft-07 for the compatibility pact to maximize existing tooling support
Parameter alias map is required; runtime will normalize using the alias map at request intake
Performance profile will include separate entries for 'interactive' (low latency) and 'throughput' (batched) modes
Golden-output fingerprints will be hashed with a stable canonicalization step; we will not store full golden outputs by default (privacy)
